column1: # Malay | English | role | usage note | root (optional)
yang|that / who / which|connector|Links a noun to a description or clause; its translation depends on the sentence.
dan|and|connector|Connects words, phrases, or clauses.
di|at / in / on|preposition|Marks location. Written separately from the following word; do not confuse it with the passive prefix di-.
tak|not|function|Everyday short form of tidak, mainly for verbs and adjectives.|tidak
boleh|can / may|function|Expresses ability or permission, depending on context.
dengan|with / by|preposition|Introduces accompaniment, manner, or an instrument.
untuk|for / to|preposition|Expresses purpose or intended recipient, depending on context.
ini|this|function|Normally follows the noun: buku ini means this book.
dalam|inside / in|preposition|Describes being inside something; di dalam is a common location phrase.
dari|from|preposition|Commonly used for places, directions, and times.
orang|person / people|object|Can refer to a person or people; number depends on context.
aku|I / me (informal)|subject|Familiar or intimate pronoun. Saya is safer with strangers.
tapi|but (conversational)|connector|Everyday short form of tetapi.|tetapi
kau|you (very familiar)|subject|Use with care: can sound rough or overly familiar. A name, title, or awak may be more appropriate.
nak|want / going to (conversational)|function|Common short form of hendak; interpretation depends on context.|hendak
adalah|is / are (formal linking word)|function|Used in some formal predicate constructions. Do not insert it into every English be sentence.
ke|to / towards|preposition|Marks destination or direction. Ke taman means to the park.
semua|all / everyone|function|Describes the whole set.
ada|exist / be present / have|verb|Expresses existence or possession depending on the construction.
pada|at / on|preposition|Often used with times or abstract relationships; usage differs from di.
apa|what|question|A question word. Apa ini? means What is this?
lagi|again / more / still|function|Its meaning depends on position and context.
buat|do / make|verb|Common conversational verb; membuat is a standard active form.
dah|already (conversational)|aspect|Everyday short form of sudah.|sudah
bukan|not (identity / noun phrase)|function|Often negates noun phrases. Saya bukan guru means I am not a teacher.
jadi|become / so|verb|Can express becoming; conversationally also used as a connector.
mana|where / which|question|Used in questions about a place or a choice.
itu|that|function|Normally follows the noun: buku itu means that book.
tidak|not|function|Usually negates verbs or adjectives; tak is common in conversation.
anda|you (formal / public address)|subject|Common in instructions, advertisements, and formal public address.
kepada|to (a recipient)|preposition|Often introduces the person receiving something.
daripada|from / than|preposition|Used for sources, comparisons, and materials, among other constructions.
ialah|is / are (identification)|function|A linking word used for identification, especially in formal contexts.
ia|it / he / she (written)|subject|More associated with writing than everyday use of dia.
telah|already / completed action|aspect|A formal marker indicating that an action has occurred.
baik|good / well|adjective|Can describe quality or condition; context affects the English rendering.
lebih|more|function|Common in comparisons: lebih besar means bigger.
mereka|they / them|subject|A plural third-person pronoun; verbs do not change to agree with it.
sekolah|school|object|A place for learning.
satu|one|number|A number; also appears in expressions referring to a single item.
jangan|do not (instruction)|function|Introduces a negative command or request.
tahu|know|verb|Refers to knowing information; kenal is used for familiarity with people or places.
hari|day|object|Hari ini means today.
juga|also / too|function|Adds something to what has already been said.
rasa|feel / taste|verb|Can refer to a feeling, an opinion, or tasting, depending on context.
kalau|if (common conversational)|connector|Introduces a condition.
ni|this (conversational)|function|Everyday short form of ini.|ini
atau|or|connector|Connects alternatives.
bagi|give / for|verb|Has several uses; beri is another common verb for give.
anak|child|object|Can refer to a child or offspring.
lain|other / different|adjective|Describes something different or another item.
tu|that (conversational)|function|Everyday short form of itu.|itu
cakap|speak / say (conversational)|verb|Common everyday verb for speaking.
seorang|one person / a person|function|A classifier expression for people; combines se- with orang.|orang
seperti|like / such as|preposition|Introduces a comparison or an example.
akan|will / future intention|aspect|Marks a future action or intention in suitable contexts.
keluar|go out / come out|verb|A movement verb; the direction depends on perspective.
menjadi|become|verb|A derived form related to jadi.|jadi
selamat|safe / well|adjective|Also used in greetings such as selamat pagi.
macam|like / kind (conversational)|function|Common in everyday comparisons; seperti is a standard alternative in many contexts.
sama|same / equal|adjective|Can describe sameness; some conversational constructions use it differently.
kawan|friend|object|A common everyday noun.
tempat|place|object|A place or location.
baru|new / just|adjective|May mean new or that something has just happened, depending on context.
lihat|see / look|verb|Root form; melihat is the standard active form.
lelaki|man / male|object|A noun or descriptor for a male person.
tiada|there is no / absent|function|Expresses absence; everyday speech also uses tak ada.
pun|also / even|function|A particle with several context-dependent uses; learn it in a phrase.
malam|night|object|Malam ini means tonight.
masuk|enter / go in|verb|A movement verb.
tahun|year|object|A unit of time.
kerana|because|connector|Introduces a reason. Sebab is also common in everyday speech.
kata|say / word|verb|Can function as a verb or noun depending on the sentence.
kan|conversational confirmation particle|function|Often seeks agreement or confirmation. It is different from the suffix -kan.
suka|like / enjoy|verb|Expresses liking or enjoyment.
tetapi|but|connector|A standard conjunction; tapi is common in conversation.
beliau|he / she (respectful)|subject|Used to refer respectfully to a person.
dua|two|number|A number; nouns usually do not require a plural ending after numbers.
hidup|live / alive / life|verb|Can be a verb, adjective, or noun depending on context.
masa|time|object|Refers to time or a period.
pergi|go|verb|The verb does not change for past tense; a time expression can make the past clear.
banyak|many / much|function|Describes a large quantity.
bila|when|question|A question word; also used in some time clauses.
dunia|world|object|The world.
hati|heart / feelings|object|Also literally the liver; many expressions concern feelings.
kena|have to / be affected by|function|An everyday word with several constructions; learn its meaning in context.
mempunyai|have / possess (formal)|verb|A standard written verb for possession; everyday constructions often use ada.
mak|mum (conversational)|object|Everyday form of emak.|emak
pernah|ever / have done before|aspect|Refers to an experience at some time before now.
salah|wrong / mistaken|adjective|Describes an error or something incorrect.
atas|top / above|preposition|Di atas means on or above; ke atas means upwards or onto.
besar|big / large|adjective|Adjectives commonly follow the noun: rumah besar means a big house.
memang|indeed / really|function|Emphasises that something is the case.
bersama|together / with|preposition|Related to sama; often expresses being together.|sama
kampung|village / hometown|object|Can refer to a village or one's home area.
rumah|house / home|object|A common destination or location.
sebab|reason / because|connector|Common in conversation for giving a reason.
beberapa|several / a few|function|A quantity word used before nouns.
kawasan|area|object|An area or region.
nama|name|object|Nama saya ... means My name is ...
bahawa|that (introducing a statement)|connector|Often used in formal reported statements; not the demonstrative itu.
jalan|road / way|object|Related to berjalan, to walk; the bare word also has conversational verbal uses.
kenapa|why (everyday)|question|Common in conversation; mengapa is a standard alternative.
sekarang|now|time|Expresses the present time.
kali|time / occasion|object|Used when counting occurrences: dua kali means twice.
masih|still|aspect|Expresses a continuing situation.
ya|yes|function|A positive response or acknowledgement.
hanya|only|function|Limits the statement to a particular thing.
lama|long (time) / old|adjective|Describes duration or age depending on context.
oleh|by|preposition|Appears in agent phrases, particularly with passive constructions.
sayang|love / affection / dear|verb|Can express affection; meaning depends on the construction.
sudah|already|aspect|Often signals that an action has happened or a state has changed.
hendak|want / intend|function|Nak is the common conversational short form.
emak|mother / mum|object|Mak is a common everyday short form.
berjalan|walk|verb|Ber- + jalan. Here ber- forms an intransitive verb, rather than marking tense.|jalan
taman|park / garden|object|Ke taman means to the park; di taman means at the park.
sana|there|function|Ke sana means to there; di sana means there as a location.
semalam|yesterday / last night|time|Context distinguishes yesterday from last night.
gembira|happy|adjective|An adjective can be a predicate without an English-style be verb: awak gembira.
kelas|class / classroom|object|In context, di dalam kelas can mean in the classroom.
guru|teacher|object|A person who teaches.
kucing|cat|object|A common animal noun.
anjing|dog|object|A common animal noun.
melompat|jump|verb|MeN- + lompat; the prefix surfaces as me- here.|lompat
lompat|jump (root)|verb|A root associated with melompat, the standard active form.
katil|bed|object|The Malaysian Malay word for bed.
lapar|hungry|adjective|An adjective predicate needs no be verb: saya lapar.
teruja|excited|adjective|Describes excitement or enthusiasm.
nampak|see / be visible (everyday)|verb|A common conversational word whose interpretation depends on the construction.
makanan|food|object|Related to makan; here -an forms a noun.|makan
melihat|see / look|verb|MeN- + lihat forms a standard active verb; it does not itself mark tense.|lihat
meja|table|object|A common household object.
panas|hot|adjective|Usually follows a noun when describing it: air panas means hot water.
sejuk|cold / cool|adjective|Describes low temperature or a cool condition.
sedap|tasty / delicious|adjective|A common everyday description of food or drink.
cantik|beautiful / pretty|adjective|A common adjective.
kecil|small|adjective|Commonly follows the noun it describes.
hari ini|today|time|A two-word time expression: literally this day.
esok|tomorrow|time|A time expression can indicate a future event without changing the verb.
pagi|morning|time|Pagi ini means this morning.
petang|afternoon / early evening|time|Usage follows local divisions of the day.
di sini|here|preposition|A two-word location phrase; ke sini means to here.
di sana|there|preposition|A location phrase; ke sana expresses movement to there.
melompat-lompat|jump repeatedly / bounce around|verb|Reduplication here expresses repeated jumping; it does not mark tense.|melompat
